description.narrative: Improve the living conditions of people affected by the crisis, starting with the most vulnerable, protect people affected by crisis and ensure respect for human rights and decrease excess mortality and morbidity among the affected population.

title.narrative: Number of adaptations in the design and/or implementation of the JR, as a result of the input from beneficiaries.

description.narrative: Active participation of beneficiaries could lead to concrete proposals in programme design and/or on how to improve existing implementation. In the activity description/comment field, indicate how this input from beneficiaries is gathered (planned) and at mid/end-term stage, what input was received from beneficiaries and to which adaptations this has led.

comment.narrative: The project will carry out close follow-up and monitoring of feedback from communities and partners during implementation. Feedback will be obtained through the quarterly engagement meetings mentioned above, through the toll-free feedback hotline number, and throgh exit interviews carried out at supported health facilities. The observed input/feedback will be documented and reviewed on a monthly basis in order to make necessary adjustments in a timely manner.

title.narrative: Number of crisis-affected people who are also involved in the design, implementation, monitoring and/or evaluation of the programme

description.narrative: Participation is defined as the involvement of crisis-affected people in one or more phases of the programme: assessment, design, implementation, monitoring or evaluation. Participation does not take place when activities are carried out in exchange for a salary of 'in-kind' payment unless the affected people are involved in decision-making processes and have an impact on decisions that affect them. Please describe in the actvity description what this involvement specifically entails and in which phase of the program conflict-affected people are involved.

comment.narrative: Medair and local partners will be keen to engage target communities including beneficiaries, community leaders, women leaders village committees and local authorities from Karan and Daynile to be involved at the initial needs assessment. Quarterly meetings will be held during implementation to monitor, discuss progress, possible adjustment based on identified gaps through dialogue with the affected communities. The project will target a total of 606 people to participate each year.

title.narrative: % of beneficiaries reporting that humanitarian assistance is delivered in a safe, accessible, accountable, and participatory manner

description.narrative: The purpose of this indicator is to facilitate the operationalisation of protection mainstreaming and provide a way to measure the identification, implementation and monitoring of required corrective actions/measures. The indicator is therefore a process indicator rather than an outcome indicator. This means that the difference between the value at the beginning (baseline) and at the end of the action (target) is not be the focus

comment.narrative: Protection mainstreaming incorporated throughout multisector activities described.

Number of people enabled to meet their basic food needs

Any kind of transfer modality (in-kind, voucher, cash) and combination thereof with objective to ensure immediate access to the necessary food commodities. This may include supplementary foods provided alongside general distribution for vulnerable people.

title.narrative: % of target persons who report improvement in their mental health and psychosocial well-being

description.narrative:
Dimensions of mental health and/or wellbeing include ((as per IASC MHPSS Framework): 1) improved functioning (e.g. the ability to carry out essential activities for daily living); 2) improved subjective wellbeing (e.g. positive emotions, self-concept, life satisfaction, hopefulness); 3)Reduced distress and/or mental, neurological or substance use disorders (or symptoms thereof); 4) Improved ability of people with mental health and psychosocial problems to cope with problems (e.g. through skills in communication, stress management, problem-solving, conflict management or vocational skills); 5) Improved social behaviour (e.g. reduced aggression); 6) Improved social connectedness (e.g. increased quality and number of connections an individual has with other people in their social circles of family, friends and acquintances)
To be measured at target group level.

comment.narrative: This indicator will measure the reported improvement in well-being among those who receive MHPSS as part of the SGBV care pathway. Related activities are described under HEA-I2 and HEA-I8

description.narrative: Health facility rehabilitated: - physical conditions of the facility prevents/limits the spread of nosocomial infections - the facility is safe (e.g. against natural hazards) - WASH services available respecting standards - storage conditions for medical supplies are according to norms. - Medical waste is disposed of according to standards. Use this sub-sector and indicator only if the project contributed substantially to the rehabilitation.

comment.narrative: Support for minor health facility rehabilitation(fences, roof, windows and doors) and maintenance of waste management facilities, water piping systems and storage, handwashing facilities, and painting and maintenance of latrines at 2 health facilities in Karan District and 1 health facility in Daynile District (based on the specific needs of each facility) by Medair during the 3 year project period

description.narrative: Number of SGBV victims that receive a comprehensive package of medical and paramedical services within 72 hours of the assault. In case SGBV victims receive medical services after 72 hours of the assualt, please indicate the number of victims supported in the activity description field.

comment.narrative: Provision of clinical management of rape services, including integragted PSS for SGBV, through the 3 supported HFs in Karan and Deynile ( Nagele HF, Jahmuriya in Karan and Caawiye HF in Deynile)

title.narrative: Number of primary health care consultations

description.narrative: Number of curative consultations provided either through existing facilities which received substantial support through the project or through parallel, self-standing emergency facilities.

comment.narrative: Support for free outpatient curative consultations at two supported HFs in Karan. To ensure the quality of the offered PHC services, these HFs will be supported with the procurement and supply of essential medicines and other medical equipment, staff incentives, capacity building in clinical skills for health staff, technical support through routine supervision by Medair Health supervisors, and joint supportive supervision with the Ministry of Health.

description.narrative: Number of hospitalisations at secondary healthcare facilities which received substantial amount of support through the project.

comment.narrative: Referrals of severe cases that cannot be treated at supported primary health care facilities and require secondary or tertiary care. These cases will include obstetric emergency cases and SAM cases with medical conditions. The referral support for obstetric emergencies will cover 2 PHC facilities in Karan where 24/7 skilled delivery is supported, while the referral support for SAM cases with medical complications will cover Karan and Daynile. The project anticipates to cumulatively support 670 serious cases throughout the project period.

description.narrative: Number of psychological and/or psychiatric consultations provided by a skilled provider. Skilled provider: medical or paramedical degree with supplementary training on mental health

comment.narrative: Mental health consultation, including treatment of mental, neurological, and substance use disorders (MNS) at supported HFs in Karan-Negeley and Jamhuriya using mhGAP-HIG and Somalia national treatment guidelines. PSS for SGBV cases will also be provided. Medair will train 6 healthcare staff on mhGAP-HIG and ensure referral linkage to primary healthcare facilities and mental health specialists.

title.narrative: Number of live births attended by skilled health personnel

description.narrative: Skilled health personnel: doctors, nurses or midwives trained in providing life-saving obstetric care, including in giving the necessary supervision, care and advice to women during pregnancy, childbirth and the postpartum period, and trained to conduct deliveries on their own, and to care for new-borns. In case this concerns trained Traditional Birth Attendants, please state this explicitly in your activity description.

comment.narrative: Support 24/7 maternity services (skilled, antenatal clinics, postnatal visits, vaccination for pregnant women as well as newborn care) at 2 health facilities in Karan District. During the 3-year implementation period, it is expected that 13,925 pregnant women will be assisted in delivering safely by trained health professionals. The project anticipates implementing this activity continually throughout the three years in the same HFs. Refresh training for 12 Midwives on BeMONc and Essential Newborn care by Medair every year during the 3-year project period.

title.narrative: Number of national and local actors supported with capacity-building

description.narrative: Please mention here the total number of national and local actors that received capacity-building support during implementation. In case more than one individual from a national/local actor participate in the capacity building activities, please only count this actor once. Note that this does not include local offices of INGOs.

comment.narrative: Medair Health Facility supervisors based at health facilities will carryout on-the-job traning and coaching for partner health facility staff on daily and on a bi-weekly basis by sector managers. Medair will coodicate with Ministry of health (MoH) and provide other training including IMAM, BeMONc, Rational Use of Drugs, mhGAP-HIG, and waste management etc annually during the 3 year project period.

title.narrative: % of budget that went to national and local actors

description.narrative: This concerns Local Implementing Partner Costs. Please divide Local Implementing Partner Costs by the Grand Total Budget (incl ICR) to calculate this percentage. Note that this does not include local offices of INGOs.

comment.narrative: Implementing partners run 2 health facilities (Karan, Daynille, including nutrition activities (10 other HF, 22 mobile outreach sites). They engage and pay the staff and utilities bills. In addition, the crisis modifier response activities will be implemented directly by the local partners. They engage in soap distributions during emergencies and water distribution at water kiosks.

title.narrative: % of budget spent on capacity building of national an local actors

description.narrative: This concerns capacity building such as training and on the job support to national and local actors. This is captured under "Capacity building local partners" in the DRA budget. Please divide Capacity building local partner costs by the Grand Total Budget (incl. ICR) to calculate this percentage. Note that this does not include local offices of INGOs.

comment.narrative: Implementing partners will utilize 5% of their direct costs for capacity strengthing on priority areas they identified (systems development) during the year 3 project period. ZAMZAM and DAWA want to acquire ERP systems for finance, procurement, human resources, payroll, and inventory management. The ERP system will handle transaction cycles from requisition to voucher payment. Consultants will oversee system installation and train key staff over the first two years. DAWA will create a website and focus on communications in year 2, while in year 3 they will work on performance management policies. Zamzam will update policies and strengthen their organization's capacity through ethics-related trainings in years 2 and 3, with donor co-funding. SAACID will utilize its 5% to establish a hotline to receive complaints, acquire HR and procurement software and hire a consultant to carry out an organisational capacity assessment. Medair will also support local partners with coaching on the job and internal trainings where needed and Help a Child will support with capacity building and coaching on Protection. At least 5% of the total direct costs will be spend on capacity building. This also includes capacity building of local staff.

title.narrative: Number of persons reached by the implementation of specific prevention measures

description.narrative:
1) Preventive measure must be built on a thorough analysis of the risks and should - as much as possible - be designed to provide concrete changes in the short/medium term. Changes must be measured in the course of the action. Preventive measure should focus on the increased risks resulting from the crisis, rather than more structural issues. 2) Use the activity description field to describe what measures are foreseen (sensitisation, infrastructure, etc.).3) Number of persons reached by prevention measures must be disaggregated by age and sex at reporting stage.4) If action also includes response activities, please add a custom indicator to reflect this.
Please note that prevention of GBV is captured under PRO-I11.

comment.narrative:
Establsihing Whats, Up groups at the 2 supported health facilities (Deynile and Karaan districts).
Year 1- 8 Whats Up parents (4 groups in Deynile, 2 Groups Nageyle and 2 groups in Karaan Districts) each composed of 15 participants (10 sessions of about 2hours each per target group) the facilitators will take the group participants through several topics such as: basics on child development, parenting skills and aware of social emotion developments).
Year 2:4 Whats Up Ladies (2 groups in Caawiye-Deynile and 2 Groups Karaan(1Jamuriya and 1 Nageyle) consisting of 20 teenage ladies each (10 sessions of about 2hours each per target group) the facilitators will take the group participants through several topics such as:awareness on risk and safe areas in the community, causes of S/GBV and consequences, how to deal with emotions.
Year 3: 4 Whats Up Children (2 groups in Caawiye-Daynile and 2 groups Karaan(1Jamuriya and 1 Nageyle) consisting of 15 Children ( 7-14 years) the facilitators will take the group participants through several topics such as:how to deal with emotions and cope with psychosocial problems resulting from many challenges eg conflict, abuse, separations

title.narrative: Number of children that received support specified to their needs

description.narrative:
1) This indicator covers response to children (girls and boys under 18). 2) Appropriate response is defined as the provision of comprehensive services/assistance based on a thorough analysis of the risks faced by persons. The protection outcome of the response must be well defined. Relevant SOPs (including functional Referral Mechanism) should be followed. 3) Use the activity description field to to describe what services (medical, MHPSS, legal, security, etc.), as well as SOPs are in place. Activities can include psychosocial support to children, Child Friendly Spaces and support to parents to fulfill their protection responsibilities towards their children. 4) Number of persons must be disaggregated by sex at reporting stage.5) If action also includes prevention activities, please describe this within the activity under this indicator.
If relevant, please specify in the activity description your target population, for example child soldiers.

comment.narrative:
Implementing and continued strengthening the existing child friendly space at Nageyle, Karaan with equipment accessible to all children including those identified with disabilities.The project will target 3,168 children each year
A total of 9,504 children will regularly engage in group and free play activities that are accessible to all children over the courses of the 3 years. The CFS will provide children an opportunity to play, grow and develop holistically. It will also provide a context for children to try new social skills and challenging new tasks, and to solve complex problems. It is expected that play will enable children to find their place in their society and culture and provide temporary relief from the hardships they face in day-to-day life.

The protection outcome of the response must be well defined. Relevant SOPs (including functional Referral Mechanism) should be followed. 3) Use the activity description field to describe what services (medical, MHPSS, legal, security, etc.), as well as SOPs in place.4) Number of persons must be disaggregated by age and sex at reporting stage.5) If action also includes prevention activities, please add a custom indicator to reflect this.
In case it concerns medical care to GBV survivors, please capture this under HEA-I8.

comment.narrative: Provision of appropriate and timely comprehensive services/assistance including pre-referral counseling (psychological support first) and medical first aid at three supported primary health facilities, and referral to other actors for Other specialized protection Service. Medair will also broaden the scope of life-saving GBV services by improving service quality in Daynile and Karaan districts through the establishments of Community protection commitees and protection caseworkers will be involved in the identification of GBV Cases, awareness raising on GBV issues in community gathering at household level and coordinate with protection caseworkers to identify GBV survivors, safe referals facilitation, follow up.

title.narrative: Number of people having access to sufficient and safe water for domestic use

description.narrative: Access: maximum distance to water point 500m, queuing time less than 15min, filling time maximum 3 min/20 litres or as locally agreed. Water access should be during the whole period of implementation unless action is mostly related to building the local water delivery capacity. Sufficient: covering basic needs, i.e. 7.5-15 l/p/d or as locally agreed. Safe: 1) low risk of faecal contamination, 2) No faecal coliforms detectable in any 100-ml sample, 3) For piped water supplies, or for all water supplies at times of risk or presence of diarrhoea epidemic, water is treated with a disinfectant to achieve free chlorine residual at the tap of 0.5 mg per litre and turbidity is below 5 NTU, 4) If for a short period, water which is contaminated chemically or radiologically is used, no (significant probability of) negative health effect is (likely to be) detected. Domestic use: drinking, cooking and personal hygiene (incl. laundry)

comment.narrative:
To reduce walking distance to water sources and to improve access to safe drinking water, Medair will continue providing water to IDPs in Daynile at 9 water kiosks (44 taps) to serve approximately 2,730 households (16,380 individuals) in Daynile IDP settlement through implementing partner (ZAMZAM) every year during the 3 year project period
To ensure safety during evening hours, installation of solar lighting at the 9 water kiosks and minor repairs for water kiosks aprons, drainage canals, replacement of the none functional/broken taps will be carried out by Medair during the 3 year project period
Refresher training for the water user committees will be carried out by ZAMZAM every year during the 3 year project period.

title.narrative: % of target population with adequate WASH services and hygiene practices

description.narrative:
Average % of the following indicators: - % of population considering that their basic WASH needs are met. - % of population with adequate hygiene practices (according to SPHERE standards on appropriate use and regular maintenance of facilities and on hand washing)
Sample size should be based on your specific target group, not on the catchment area. Standard list of questions can be found on indikit.net. Only include questions based on your intervention. For example if you do not construct latrines you cannot ask questions about access to latrines.

comment.narrative: See activities under results WSH-I1, WSH-I4, and WSH-I6 for detailed descriptions of the activities intended to improve access to safe drinking water and improve hygiene practices. This will be measured by household survey (PDM) conducted in Daynile after project activities have been completed. The target is based on an assumed average of handwashing practices and access to safe water.

title.narrative: Number of people reached with hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities

description.narrative: Hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities. Could be training, campaigns, radio broadcasts, flyers etc. Excludes the distribution of Hygiene/dignity kits that should be covered under WHS-I1.

comment.narrative:
Using the Care Group concept with 545 CG volunteers (120 Jamhuriya, 245 Negeley in Karan, and 180 in Dayniile). SOMJR will fund 365 CG volunteers in Jamhuria and Nageyle, while the remaining 180 CG volunteers in Dayniile will be funded through other grants. Each volunteer will visit 15 neighbour households on a bi-weekly basis providing messages to all household members present. The volunteers will conduct hygiene promotion messaging using CHWs MoH harmonized guideline and the Somali translated Educational and Communications (IEC) booklets also in community forums (where possible). Monthly incentives will be done through the implementing partners (DAWA and ZAMZAM during the 3 year project period.
One time incentive in year 1 will be carried out by Medair and implementing partners and in year 2 and 3 will be carried out by the implementing partners.
Refresher trainings for the volunteers will be conducted by Medair and implementing partners in year 1 while in year 2 and year 3 trainings will be conducted by the partners (DAWA-Negeley and ZAMZAM -Jamhuria-Karan district)

title.narrative: Number of people having regular access to soap to meet hygienic needs

description.narrative: Regular and timely access: 250g soap/p/m for personal hygiene, 200g soap/p/month for laundry. This includes hygiene/dignity kits. Access may be in-kind or though voucher distribution or through unconditional restricted cash to enable beneficiary to buy soap (without compromising access to other basic needs). Distributed items need to be culturally acceptable i.e. take into account local practice and expectations.

comment.narrative:
Distribution of Hygiene kit to 15,000 IDPs in Daynile District during emergencies including disease outbreaks. A total of 2500 Hygiene Distributions (833 Hygiene Kits per year). The Hygiene Kits distribution will be carried out in Daynile x 3 times during the project period by the local implementing partner (ZAMZAM) Post distribution monitoring for hygiene kits and Soap for hand demonstration will be carried after each distribution by Medair and implementing partner.
Each household will receive 1) 800grms of soap 2) 2 (20L) jerrycans 3) 100 tabs of Aqua tabs
Distribution of 200mg of soap for handwashing demonstration will be distributed to neighbour households in Karan through the 345 care group volunteers (120 in Jamhuriya through ZAMZAM and 245 in Negayle through DAWA) on a quarterly basis
